items.title: Escrow surplus refund
items.summary: Your servicer must analyze your escrow account once a year. If the analysis shows a surplus of $50 or more, the servicer must refund it to you within 30 days of the analysis. A surplus under $50 may be refunded or credited against next year's escrow payments. You must be current when the analysis is done; a payment counts as current if the servicer received it within 30 days of its due date.

fields.label: Who
fields.value: Borrowers with an escrow account on a federally related mortgage loan who are current at the time of the yearly escrow analysis. If a payment was not received within 30 days of its due date, the servicer may keep the surplus in the account under the terms of the loan documents.

fields.label: Rule
fields.value: RESPA Regulation X, 12 CFR 1024.17(f)(2) surplus, (f)(3) shortage, (f)(4) deficiency, (f)(5) notice, (i) annual statement.

fields.label: Surplus
fields.value: A surplus is the amount by which the current escrow balance exceeds the target balance. $50 or more: the servicer must refund it within 30 days from the date of the analysis. Under $50: the servicer may refund it or credit it against next year's escrow payments.

fields.label: Shortage
fields.value: A shortage is the amount by which the balance falls short of the target balance. Shortage under one month's escrow payment: the servicer may leave it, require repayment within 30 days, or require equal monthly payments over at least 12 months. Shortage of one month's payment or more: the servicer may leave it or require equal monthly payments over at least 12 months.

fields.label: Deficiency
fields.value: A deficiency is a negative escrow balance. Under one month's payment: the servicer may leave it, require repayment within 30 days, or require 2 or more equal monthly payments. One month's payment or more: the servicer may leave it or require 2 or more equal monthly payments.

fields.label: Notice
fields.value: The servicer must tell you at least once each escrow computation year if there is a shortage or deficiency. The annual escrow statement is due within 30 days after the end of the computation year and must explain how any surplus is being handled. The servicer may hold a cushion of no more than one-sixth of the estimated total annual escrow payments.

fields.label: How to ask
fields.value: Read your yearly escrow statement. If it shows a surplus of $50 or more and no refund arrived within 30 days, send the servicer a written notice of error at its designated address; the CFPB sample letter has a line for an escrow refund you did not receive. If the servicer does not fix it, submit a complaint to the CFPB online or at (855) 411-2372.

items.title: PMI cancellation and refund of unearned premiums
items.summary: Under the Homeowners Protection Act you can ask your servicer to cancel private mortgage insurance (PMI) once your loan balance reaches 80% of the home's original value. The servicer must end PMI automatically on the date the balance is scheduled to reach 78%, and in any case at the midpoint of the loan term if you are current. Premiums collected after those dates are unearned, and you may be entitled to get them back within 45 days.

fields.label: Who
fields.value: Borrower-paid PMI on a mortgage for a single-family principal residence closed on or after July 29, 1999. The CFPB says FHA and VA loans and lender-paid mortgage insurance have different requirements; ask your servicer.

fields.label: Rule
fields.value: Homeowners Protection Act of 1998, 12 U.S.C. 4901 and 4902; CFPB Compliance Bulletin 2015-03.

fields.label: Request at 80%
fields.value: Send a written cancellation request when the balance is first scheduled to reach 80% of the original value, or actually reaches 80% through extra payments. Original value is the lower of the contract sales price and the appraised value at closing; for a refinance it is the appraised value used to approve the refinance. You must be current, have a good payment history (no payment 30 or more days late in the 12 months before the cancellation date or your request, whichever is later, and none 60 or more days late in the 12 months before that), certify that there is no second mortgage or other lien on your equity, and, if the loan holder requires it, provide evidence such as an appraisal (which you may have to pay for) that the value has not fallen below the original value. Your PMI disclosure form should show the first date you can ask.

fields.label: Automatic at 78%
fields.value: If you are current, PMI ends on the date the balance is first scheduled to reach 78% of the original value under the original amortization schedule, whatever the actual balance is. If you are behind on that date, it ends on the first day of the first month after you become current. No appraisal, valuation fee or minimum loan age may be required, and extra payments do not move this date up.

fields.label: Final termination
fields.value: If PMI is still in place, it may not be required past the first day of the month after the midpoint of the loan's amortization period (for a 30-year loan, the month after the 180th payment), as long as you are current. This matters for interest-only, balloon-payment or principal-forbearance loans whose balance may never reach 78%.

fields.label: Refund
fields.value: No PMI payments may be required more than 30 days after the termination date, or more than 30 days after the later of your cancellation request and the date you met the evidence and certification requirements. Unearned premiums must be returned to you within 45 days of cancellation or termination. The CFPB says they must be returned directly to you, not left in your escrow account.

fields.label: Disclosure
fields.value: Each year the servicer must send a written statement of your right to cancel or terminate PMI, with an address and phone number to use.

fields.label: Investor rules
fields.value: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac loans may follow investor guidelines that allow earlier cancellation, for example based on current value, but those guidelines cannot cut back the rights above.

fields.label: High-risk loans
fields.value: Loans classed as high risk at closing are outside the 80% and 78% rules. For non-conforming high-risk loans, PMI ends when the balance is scheduled to reach 77% of the original value, and the midpoint rule still applies.

fields.label: How to ask
fields.value: Write to your servicer asking for cancellation under the Homeowners Protection Act and state the date your balance reaches 80% of the original value. If the servicer refuses, keeps billing past the end date, or does not return unearned premiums within 45 days, send a written notice of error and submit a complaint to the CFPB online or at (855) 411-2372.

items.title: Mortgage payoff: statement, escrow refund and lien release
items.summary: Ask in writing for your payoff amount and the servicer must send an accurate payoff statement within a reasonable time and in no case more than 7 business days. After you pay the loan off, any money left in your escrow account must be returned within 20 days (not counting weekends and legal public holidays), and a final escrow statement must follow within 60 days.

fields.label: Who
fields.value: Payoff statement: any consumer loan secured by a dwelling, including home equity lines of credit. Escrow refund and final statement: escrow accounts on federally related mortgage loans.

fields.label: Rule
fields.value: Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.36(c)(3) payoff statement; Regulation X, 12 CFR 1024.34(b) escrow refund and 12 CFR 1024.17(i)(4)(iii) short-year statement.

fields.label: Payoff statement
fields.value: Must state the total amount needed to pay the loan in full as of a specified date. It is due within a reasonable time and in no case more than 7 business days after the servicer receives your written request. For loans in bankruptcy or foreclosure, reverse mortgages, shared appreciation mortgages, or natural disasters, a reasonable time applies instead. The payoff can be higher than your current balance: it includes interest through the payoff date, unpaid fees, and any prepayment penalty.

fields.label: Escrow refund
fields.value: Within 20 days (excluding legal public holidays, Saturdays and Sundays) of payment in full, the servicer must return any amount left in an escrow account within its control. With your agreement it may instead credit the balance to the escrow account of a new loan, but only if the new loan is from the lender the old loan was originally payable to, from the owner of the old loan, or uses the same servicer.

fields.label: Final statement
fields.value: A short-year escrow statement must be sent within 60 days after the servicer receives the payoff funds.

fields.label: Lien release
fields.value: The CFPB says there may be a delay between paying off your mortgage and the release of the lien. State property records show whether the lien was released; contact your county recorder of deeds or local Secretary of State. Your lender should also return the original note to you, and you can ask the company that paid off the loan whether the lien was released.

fields.label: Errors
fields.value: An inaccurate payoff balance is a covered servicing error: after a written notice of error the servicer must respond within 7 days, not counting weekends and legal public holidays. The CFPB says a missing escrow refund 20 days after payoff is also a reason to send a notice of error. Servicers must keep records for at least one year after payoff.

fields.label: How to ask
fields.value: Request the payoff amount in writing. After payoff, watch for the escrow refund and the final escrow statement. If the refund does not arrive within the 20-day period, send a written notice of error to the servicer's designated address. If that fails, submit a complaint to the CFPB online or at (855) 411-2372.

items.title: Notice of error: misapplied payments, fees and escrow mistakes
items.summary: If your servicer does not apply a payment the way your loan requires, does not credit it as of the day it arrived, charges a fee it has no reasonable basis for, fails to pay taxes or insurance from escrow, or gives a wrong payoff figure, a written notice of error starts fixed deadlines: acknowledgment within 5 days and a correction or written explanation within 30 days (7 days for payoff errors), not counting weekends and legal public holidays.

fields.label: Who
fields.value: Borrowers on a mortgage loan covered by the RESPA Regulation X servicing rules.

fields.label: Rule
fields.value: Regulation X, 12 CFR 1024.35 error resolution; 12 CFR 1024.17(i) annual escrow statement; Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.36(c)(1) payments credited as of the date of receipt.

fields.label: Covered errors
fields.value: Refusing a payment that meets the servicer's written requirements; not applying an accepted payment to principal, interest, escrow or other charges as the loan and the law require; not crediting a payment as of the date of receipt; not paying taxes, insurance premiums or other escrow charges; imposing a fee the servicer lacks a reasonable basis for; giving an inaccurate payoff balance; loss-mitigation, foreclosure and servicing-transfer errors; and any other error relating to the servicing of your loan.

fields.label: Deadlines
fields.value: Written acknowledgment within 5 days. Response within 30 days; for some errors the servicer may add 15 days if it tells you in writing, with reasons, before the 30 days end. Payoff-balance errors: 7 days. Foreclosure errors: before the foreclosure sale or within 30 days, whichever is earlier. All counts exclude legal public holidays, Saturdays and Sundays.

fields.label: Outcome
fields.value: The servicer must either correct the error and tell you in writing, or do a reasonable investigation and tell you in writing that no error occurred, with the reasons and your right to request the documents it relied on. It may not charge a fee or require a payment as a condition of responding. For 60 days after receiving your notice it may not send negative information about the disputed payment to a credit reporting company.

fields.label: Annual escrow statement
fields.value: Within 30 days after the end of each escrow computation year the servicer must send an annual escrow statement with the past year's account history, a projection for the next year, and an explanation of how any surplus is being handled. If the servicer failed to pay an escrow item, the CFPB says to send a notice of error with a copy of the bill and to contact the tax authority or insurer as soon as possible.

fields.label: How to ask
fields.value: Write a letter, not on your payment coupon, with your name as it appears on the mortgage, your home address, the loan number and a specific description of the error. Mail it to the servicer's designated notice-of-error address printed on your statement, coupon book or website; the CFPB sample letter covers payment, escrow, fee and payoff errors. Keep making your payments while you wait. If the servicer does not fix it, submit a complaint to the CFPB online or at (855) 411-2372; the CFPB says most companies respond within 15 days.

items.title: Force-placed insurance: cancellation and refund
items.summary: If your servicer bought hazard insurance for your home because it believed your own policy had lapsed, it must cancel that policy within 15 days of receiving proof that you had coverage, refund every force-placed premium charge and related fee you paid for the overlapping period, and remove those charges from your account. It may not charge you at all without a first written notice at least 45 days ahead and a reminder at least 15 days ahead.

fields.label: Who
fields.value: Borrowers charged for hazard insurance that the servicer obtained on behalf of the loan's owner (force-placed insurance). Insurance the servicer renews or pays from your escrow account is not force-placed insurance under this rule.

fields.label: Rule
fields.value: RESPA Regulation X, 12 CFR 1024.37; for escrow accounts also 12 CFR 1024.17(k)(5).

fields.label: Before charging
fields.value: The servicer needs a reasonable basis to believe you failed to keep the hazard insurance your loan requires. It must deliver or mail a first written notice at least 45 days before charging you, and a reminder notice at least 30 days after the first notice and at least 15 days before charging. It may charge only if, by the end of that period, it has received no evidence that you had coverage in place. Renewing force-placed coverage also requires a notice at least 45 days before the new charge.

fields.label: Refund
fields.value: Within 15 days of receiving, from you or anyone else, evidence that you had hazard insurance in place, the servicer must cancel the force-placed policy, refund all force-placed premium charges and related fees you paid for any period of overlapping coverage, and remove those charges and fees for that period from your account.

fields.label: Charges
fields.value: All force-placed insurance charges must be bona fide and reasonable, meaning they bear a reasonable relationship to the servicer's cost of providing the service. The CFPB notes force-placed insurance usually costs more than a policy you buy and generally protects only the lender.

fields.label: Escrow accounts
fields.value: If your escrow account covers hazard insurance and you are more than 30 days behind, the servicer still may not buy force-placed insurance; it must keep your own premium paid, advancing its own funds if the account is short, unless it has a reasonable basis to believe your policy was cancelled or not renewed for a reason other than nonpayment, or that the property is vacant. It may later seek repayment of the funds it advanced.

fields.label: How to ask
fields.value: Get or reinstate your own policy, send the servicer proof of coverage, and ask it in writing to cancel the force-placed policy. If the refund has not appeared within 15 days of your proof, send a written notice of error to the servicer's designated address. If that fails, submit a complaint to the CFPB online or at (855) 411-2372.
